HUMAN SCALE / Body, gesture & creative attention

Physiognomy & metoposcopy.

Historical systems that attributed character, fate or other meanings to bodily appearance, especially facial and forehead features.

LEXICON / LANGUAGE & MEANING

Names in context.

Physiognomy
Fisiognomía

Historical interpretation of outward features as supposed signs of character or fate.

Metoposcopy
Metoposcopia

Historical readings of forehead lines and markings.

PROVENANCE & INTERPRETATION

A practice,
a setting.

Early modern manuscripts preserve elaborate correspondences for faces and forehead lines. They are documented here as historical claims; appearance does not establish a person’s character, honesty, health or destiny.

FIELD NOTE / METHOD

Keep a record.

  1. Select a dated historical diagram or text and identify its author.
  2. Describe the diagram’s categories and the claims the author makes.
  3. Compare the historical vocabulary without applying character judgments to a living person.
POTPOURRI / PHOTO GUIDE

What to include.

  • Use a permitted image of the historical page with its caption and page number.
  • Provide a close view of the diagram’s labels and its catalog reference.
